$$J_{X^{\mathrm{an}}}[\eta_A]=\rho_{X^{\mathrm{an}}}\bigl(c_1(A)\bigr),$$
where $J$ is the de Rham comparison and $\rho$ the change of coefficients
$\mathbb Z\to\mathbb R$
([[lem-rational-cohomology-scalar-comparison-for-compact-smooth-manifolds]]).
In dimension $n=0$ and for $X=\varnothing$ every $2$-form and every degree-two
cohomology class is zero and $\eta_A=0$, so the identity holds trivially.

Assume AC. For a compact Kähler manifold $X$ in the sense of
[[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]], every de
Rham class has a unique smooth harmonic representative and
$$H^k(X;\mathbb C)=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}H^{p,q}(X),\qquad \overline{H^{p,q}(X)}=H^{q,p}(X).$$
Here $H^{p,q}(X)$ is precisely the set of classes with a $d$-closed smooth
representative of type $(p,q)$, so the decomposition is independent of the
Kähler metric. Writing $\Omega_X^p$ for the sheaf of holomorphic $p$-forms (the
kernel of $\bar\partial$ on the sheaf $\mathcal A^{p,0}$ of smooth $(p,0)$-forms),
$H^{p,q}(X)$ is isomorphic to $H^q(X,\Omega_X^p)$, the sheaf cohomology of
[[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]. The Hodge filtration
$F^a=\bigoplus_{p\ge a}H^{p,k-p}$ of $H^k(X;\mathbb C)$ equals the filtration
induced by the holomorphic-degree filtration of the de Rham complex, whose
spectral sequence has $E_1^{p,q}=H^q(X,\Omega_X^p)$ and degenerates at $E_1$.
Pullback by holomorphic maps of compact Kähler manifolds and cup product
preserve Hodge type, so $H^k(X;\mathbb Q)$ is a functorial rational pure Hodge
structure.

Assume AC. For a compact smooth manifold $X$, the natural coefficient maps
induce isomorphisms $H^k(X;\mathbb Q)\otimes_{\mathbb Q}F\cong H^k(X;F)$ for
every characteristic-zero field $F$, finite-dimensional in each degree. For
$F=\mathbb R,\mathbb C$ these identify singular cohomology with the real or
complex de Rham cohomology. They preserve cup products and are natural for maps
between such manifolds. No ordered-field or positivity structure is asserted
for a general $F$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), inherited from the
analytic suppliers below. Let $X$ be a compact Kähler $n$-fold with Kähler form
$\omega$, in the conventions of
[[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]], and put
$L=[\omega]\smile(-)$ on cohomology. Then the following hold.

- $L^{n-k}:H^k(X;\mathbb R)\to H^{2n-k}(X;\mathbb R)$ is an isomorphism for
  $0\le k\le n$.
- Harmonic representatives transport $(L,\Lambda,H)$ to an $\mathfrak{sl}_2$
  action: $L$ is cup product with $[\omega]$, $\Lambda$ on cohomology means
  applying $\Lambda$ to the harmonic representative and not to an arbitrary
  closed form, $H$ acts by $\deg-n$, and
  $[L,\Lambda]=H$, $[H,L]=2L$, $[H,\Lambda]=-2\Lambda$ hold on cohomology.
- Primitive cohomology is
  $P^k=\{a\in H^k(X;\mathbb R):\text{the harmonic representative of }a\text{ lies in }\ker\Lambda\}$,
  and for $0\le k\le n$ one has
  $P^k=\ker\bigl(L^{n-k+1}:H^k(X;\mathbb R)\to H^{2n-k+2}(X;\mathbb R)\bigr)$;
  for every $k$,
  $$H^k(X;\mathbb R)=\bigoplus_{r\ge\max(0,k-n)}L^rP^{k-2r},$$
  and a class of type $(p,q)$ has primitive components of type $(p-r,q-r)$.
- If $[\omega]$ is the real image of a rational class
  $\ell\in H^2(X;\mathbb Q)$, all these decompositions and $L$-isomorphisms are
  rational, and they remain isomorphisms after extension to every
  characteristic-zero field.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), inherited from the
analytic suppliers below. Let $X$ be a compact Kähler $n$-fold in the
conventions of
[[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]], with
Kähler form $\omega$, and let $0\le k\le n$. On the primitive space $P^k$ put
$$Q_k(a,b)=\epsilon(k)\int_Xa\wedge b\wedge\omega^{n-k},$$
where $a,b$ are closed smooth representatives of the classes and the integral
is independent of the representatives. This form is $(-1)^k$-symmetric, pairs
$P^{p,q}$ only with $P^{q,p}$, and for nonzero $a\in P^{p,q}$ satisfies
$$i^{p-q}Q_k(a,\bar a)=(n-k)!\,\|a_{\mathrm{harm}}\|_{L^2}^2>0.$$
If $[\omega]=\ell\in H^2(X;\mathbb Q)$, then $Q_k$ is a rational polarization
of $P^k$, and full $H^k$ is polarized by the orthogonal direct sum form $S_k$
that on $L^rP^{k-2r}$ is $(-1)^rQ_k$, equivalently
$S_k(L^ru,L^rv)=Q_{k-2r}(u,v)$ for $u,v\in P^{k-2r}$; degrees $k>n$ are
polarized by transporting the polarization of $H^{2n-k}$ along $L^{k-n}$, with
Tate shift. For every real Kähler class the same positivity and nondegeneracy
statements hold, without rationality. In particular this applies to smooth
closed complex projective submanifolds of projective space with a hyperplane
polarization, hence to smooth projective complex varieties through their smooth
projective analytifications; more generally it applies to every real Kähler
class, including $\ell+\epsilon\eta$ when represented by a positive closed
form. For any continuous family of Kähler classes the primitive kernels (of
every fixed degree $0\le k\le n$) vary continuously as subspaces; rational
primitive spaces are asserted only at rational classes.

Let $(V,Q)$ be a polarized rational pure Hodge structure and $U\subseteq V$ a
rational sub-Hodge structure, with the notions of
[[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]] and
[[def-morphisms-and-polarizability-of-rational-hodge-structures]]. Then $Q|_U$
is a polarization of $U$, and
$$V=U\oplus U^{\perp_Q},\qquad U^{\perp_Q}=\{x\in V:Q(x,U)=0\}$$
is an orthogonal direct sum of rational Hodge structures in which the
complement is polarized. Every short exact sequence of polarizable rational
pure Hodge structures of a fixed weight splits in the category of Hodge
structures, and every polarizable rational pure Hodge structure is a finite
direct sum of simple Hodge structures. These are claims about rational Hodge
substructures; they do not assert a splitting for an arbitrary local
subsystem. Every rational splitting and direct-sum decomposition of this item
is given by rational matrices satisfying the linear identities recorded below,
and those identities, hence the splitting and the decomposition, persist after
extension of scalars to every characteristic-zero field; no positivity or
order structure is asserted over that field, and no subobject of the extension
is claimed to be rationally defined.

derivations.claim: By [F1] the analytification $X^{\mathrm{an}}$ is a compact Kähler manifold of dimension $n$, and the ample class $\ell$ is the real image of an integral class represented by a positive closed real $(1,1)$-form, so $\ell$ is a real Kähler class and has Hodge type $(1,1)$ in the Hodge structure of [F2]. By [F2] each rational cohomology space $H^k(X;\mathbb Q)$ is finite-dimensional and pure Hodge of weight $k$, pullback along holomorphic maps of analytifications is a morphism of Hodge structures because it preserves the type decomposition, and cup product has Hodge type $(0,0)$ since the wedge of forms of types $(p,q)$ and $(r,s)$ has type $(p+r,q+s)$; the rational structure and its scalar extensions are those of the comparison [F2].

Apply the hard-Lefschetz and primitive-decomposition theorem [F3] to $X^{\mathrm{an}}$ with the Kähler class $\ell$: the maps $\ell^{n-k}:H^k\to H^{2n-k}$ are isomorphisms for $0\le k\le n$, the primitive spaces are $P^k=\ker\ell^{n-k+1}$ in those degrees, the decomposition $H^k=\bigoplus_{r\ge\max(0,k-n)}\ell^rP^{k-2r}$ holds in every degree, a class of type $(p,q)$ has primitive components of type $(p-r,q-r)$, and all of this data is rational because $\ell$ is rational. For $k>n$ the complementary degree $2n-k$ satisfies $0\le 2n-k<n$, so hard Lefschetz in that degree gives that $\ell^{n-(2n-k)}=\ell^{k-n}:H^{2n-k}\to H^k$ is an isomorphism, the inverse of the displayed map; its inverse is likewise rational.

By the Hodge–Riemann theorem [F4] applied to the same compact Kähler manifold, the rational primitive summands of step 2.1 satisfy the displayed Hodge–Riemann positivity and the sign-adjusted full cohomology pairing is a rational polarization of $H^k$, with the transport from the complementary degree $\le n$ and the Tate shift in degrees $k>n$; the same absolute positivity and hard-Lefschetz statements hold for every real Kähler class, and the primitive kernels of each fixed degree vary continuously along a continuous family of Kähler classes [F4]. By the orthogonal-splitting lemma [F5] every rational sub-Hodge structure of $H^k$ splits off orthogonally with polarized complement, every short exact sequence of polarizable rational Hodge structures splits, and every polarizable structure is a finite direct sum of simple ones. The rationality statements of step 2.1 and of this step are rational linear identities (nonzero rational determinants, rational idempotent projections, rational matrices of the Lefschetz isomorphisms), so by [F5] they persist under extension of scalars to every characteristic-zero field. No supplier in [F3, F4, F5] asserts or uses weak hyperplane Lefschetz, relative hard Lefschetz, singular intersection-cohomology purity or semisimplicity of arbitrary local systems, so this package supplies none of them.
